factual_methodology.summary: Reconciled DOL 22 Oct weekly initial/insured claims against the official release; BLS Sept payrolls; NBS Chinese Q3 GDP breakdown; final Eurostat Sept HICP energy contributions; EIA Oct 16 inventory/product balances; IBGE Sept IPCA; IMF Oct forecasts. Stocks, weekly flows, survey definitions and vintages differentiated; DOL and IBGE official source links corrected.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: New 22 Oct low-layoff versus slow-hiring evidence is distinguishable from 21 Oct UK inflation/sovereign-finance paper; international monetary/real-income, energy and Chinese composition mechanisms addressed; no unverifiable 22 October asset closing prices.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Three quantitative bar charts for US initial claims, crude inventories and China's sectoral output; data figures identical across EN and PT-BR. Multiple tables, causal flow, qualitative exposure map and unit/period caveats.

research_depth.summary: Six analytical sections contrast labor flows versus benefit stock, regional oil inventory differences, Chinese industry/construction divergence and non-additive price indices. Explicit conditional scenarios and observable falsifiers.

evidence_traceability.summary: Nine matching references across both languages from DOL, BLS, NBS, Eurostat, EIA, IBGE, IMF and Federal Reserve; main reported figures cross-checked with current 2026 institutional releases. IBGE index page is a general source rather than report-specific release.

counterfactual_review.summary: Low claims could reflect labor hoarding or underlying resilience, not weak demand alone; insured stock may change with eligibility and processing. Oil draw does not identify demand without full balance; China industry growth may not spread to construction/consumption.

contrary_evidence: Low new unemployment claims could reflect robust retention rather than unemployment duration deterioration; benefits claimants are not the entire jobless population.
A crude stock draw can result from imports, refinery throughput, exports or disruptions rather than stronger end demand.
Chinese manufacturing output growth and construction contraction do not establish causality or automatically determine trade gains elsewhere.
limitations: Labor claims have weekly coverage and eligibility restrictions; payrolls and unemployment are separate monthly surveys.
EIA weekly petroleum disposition estimates are not audited end-use consumption or global flow totals.
Country inflation rates reflect incompatible baskets and time horizons. IMF projections use statistical information principally through 1 October.
The IBGE reference links to its general indicators portal; direct machine access to this portal was restricted in external retrieval.
This is internal publication QA of selected original-source evidence and inference, not independent external peer review.
notes: Bilingual text numbers, graphic data and institutional source URLs verified by direct comparison; selected October primary-source releases reviewed; no synthetic price or currency quotes, no global stock/flow conflation.

en.title: Global Macro — Low US layoffs meet weak hiring, uneven Chinese growth and an energy-driven inflation divide
en.deck: US initial claims fall to 194,000 while continuing insured unemployment rises; China's manufacturing diverges from construction and European inflation remains energy-led.

producer_checks.editorial_novelty: Fresh divergence between declining initial US unemployment claims and increasing continuing insured unemployment, assessed against September weak payrolls, China's 21 October Q3 sectoral GDP and energy-inflation incidence across euro area and Brazil. Distinct from UK CPI/debt of 21 October.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Each locale: three reproducible explicit quantitative bar charts, three substantive tables, one multichain flow and one geographic exposure map.
producer_checks.source_check: Nine identical primary source URLs from US DOL, BLS, EIA, Chinese NBS, Eurostat, IBGE, IMF and Federal Reserve. Distinct release dates, stock/flow concepts, geographies and forecast versus observation are identified.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: Same official numeric facts, matching nine citation URLs and three identical numeric chart series in EN and PT-BR; conditional scenarios, counterfactuals and caveats parallel.
